answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks with reputation staking that vests slowly over time. Each identity locks collateral accruing influence only with age, so a freshly spawned fake starts at its nadir of trust: no stake age, no voting weight. Attackers minting ten thousand clones watch them freeze in the tundra of zero weight unless each is funded and aged, making attack cost linear in identities. Honest peers earn slashing-backed reputation and form a harbor of mutual attestation: newcomers need vouches from established agents, and a voucher's stake is slashed if its agent misbehaves.
